pharm-e2-diabetes-11-065.prompt: How do sulfonylureas increase insulin secretion?
pharm-e2-diabetes-11-065.answer: They close beta-cell ATP-sensitive K+ channels.
pharm-e2-diabetes-11-065.why:
They need functioning beta cells and may cause hypoglycemia.
This is an insulin alternative. (dont do it)

pharm-e2-diabetes-11-077.prompt: Why does severe insulin resistance increase EMS (Equine Metabolic Syndrome) laminitis risk?
pharm-e2-diabetes-11-077.answer: Sustained hyperinsulinemia can damage lamellar function.
pharm-e2-diabetes-11-077.why: The link is endocrinopathic laminitis, not always hyperglycemia.

pharm-e2-43.prompt: Why can fructosamine be useful in stressed cats?
pharm-e2-43.answer: It's a one-time test that avoids the stress response in cats. Provides an indirect measurement of blood glucose over 2-3 weeks.
pharm-e2-43.why: One clinic glucose sample may be raised by stress. Typically, recurrent samples are needed to properly diagnose DM.

pharm-l10-quick-004.prompt: Why must insulin concentration and delivery device match?
pharm-l10-quick-004.answer:
U-40 and U-100 products require compatible dosing equipment to avoid dose errors.
Insulin has a very narrow safety margin. Proper pens ensure that the correct dose and concentration is administered to avoid under or overdosing.
pharm-l10-quick-004.why: Mismatched devices can cause dangerous under- or overdosing.

pharm-e2-diabetes-10-036.prompt: Which insulin analog has very prolonged duration? What species can it be an option for if insulin glargine is unavailable?
pharm-e2-diabetes-10-036.answer: Degludec. Up to 48 hours and possible to be used in cats.
pharm-e2-diabetes-10-036.why:
Long duration does not automatically make it the best choice for each patient.
It is an insulin analog and fatty acid with muli hexamers. Comes in a pen only form. Very few glucose nadirs (only one low point)
pharm-e2-diabetes-10-036.slide: Course Lectures 10–11 (user notes), 2026 AAHA/FDA safety check

pharm-e2-diabetes-10-021.prompt: What is the duration category of Vetsulin?
pharm-e2-diabetes-10-021.why:
It contains amorphous and crystalline insulin zinc fractions.
Dogs first choice. Lente means slow, makes it longer acting.
pharm-e2-diabetes-10-021.slide: Course Lectures 10–11 (user notes), 2026 AAHA/FDA safety check

pharm-e2-diabetes-11-072.prompt: How does propylene glycol help treat bovine ketosis?
pharm-e2-diabetes-11-072.answer: It supplies gluconeogenic precursors after metabolism.
pharm-e2-diabetes-11-072.why:
Dietary and concurrent-disease management are also important.
It becomes propionate, a glucose precursor, plus a corticosteroid, which stimulates gluconeogenesis (C3+C3=C6). If severe, IV gluoce then PZI every other day.
pharm-e2-diabetes-11-072.slide: Course Lectures 10–11 (user notes), 2026 AAHA/FDA safety check

pharm-e2-thyroid12-025.prompt: Why is methimazole stopped before some I-131 treatments?
pharm-e2-thyroid12-025.answer: To allow appropriate iodine uptake and thyroid assessment. Also the patient cannot be touched for at least 3 days and needs to be stable.
pharm-e2-thyroid12-025.why: Withdrawal timing varies by treatment facility; follow its protocol.

pharm-e2-thyroid12-016.prompt: Why avoid switching levothyroxine brands without monitoring?
pharm-e2-thyroid12-016.why: Recheck thyroid values and clinical response after a formulation change. So always confirm with brand your clinic has.
pharm-e2-thyroid12-016.slide: Lecture 12 · user notes, reviewed alongside course treatment notes

pharm-e2-51.prompt: Why might a sick dog have low T4 without hypothyroidism?
pharm-e2-51.answer: Nonthyroidal illness or drug effects can reduce measured hormone.
pharm-e2-51.why:
Thyroid hormone sets the pace of metabolism, so lowering it during illness saves energy and protein when the animal is not eating, is catabolic, and needs its reserves to fight the problem. Fasting alone produces the same pattern, which supports this.
So always check after they have recovered.

pharm-e2-autonomic13-015.prompt: What is prazosin's mechanism and urinary indication?
pharm-e2-autonomic13-015.answer: α1 antagonist; reduces urethral smooth-muscle tone thus promoting urination
pharm-e2-autonomic13-015.why: It may help functional urethral outflow resistance; it cannot remove a urethral stone.

pharm-e2-autonomic13-025.prompt: How does pilocarpine change pupil size?
pharm-e2-autonomic13-025.why:

pharm-e2-autonomic13-020.prompt: Why is bethanechol unsafe with urethral obstruction?
pharm-e2-autonomic13-020.answer: It increases pressure against a blocked urinary outlet, since this is to promote urination.
pharm-e2-autonomic13-020.why: A detrusor stimulant does not relax or remove an obstructing lesion.

pharm-e2-autonomic13-017.answer: Phenoxybenzamine is an irreversible, nonselective α blockade versus prazosins reversible α1 blockade.

pharm-e2-59.why: Outlet relaxation differs from stimulating the bladder wall. Nonselective so it can cause some cardiovascular side effects.

pharm-e2-autonomic13-014.prompt: What is oxybutynin's mechanism and clinical effect? Urine retention.
pharm-e2-autonomic13-014.why: It supports bladder storage and can worsen urinary retention if outflow is blocked.

pharm-e2-autonomic13-012.prompt: What is phenylpropanolamine's main urinary effect?
pharm-e2-autonomic13-012.answer: Increases urethral closure pressure through sympathomimetic action (A1 and B1 agonist), thus causing urinary retention
pharm-e2-autonomic13-012.why: It is used for selected canine urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence.

pharm-e2-autonomic13-016.prompt: What is tamsulosin's mechanism and urinary indication?
pharm-e2-autonomic13-016.answer: Relatively α1A-selective antagonist; relaxes urethral outlet thus can be used for urinary retention
pharm-e2-autonomic13-016.why: Used for functional urethral spasm or increased smooth-muscle resistance.

pharm-e2-cardio14-011.prompt: What cardiac adverse effect can positive inotropes cause?
pharm-e2-cardio14-011.why:
Higher intracellular calcium or altered excitability may provoke abnormal rhythms.
These drugs are working to treat congestive heart failure by increasing intra-myocytic calcium to improve contractility.

pharm-e2-cardio14-020.answer: β1 and β2 nonselective adrenergic receptors. (Class 2)
pharm-e2-cardio14-020.why:
β1 blockade slows cardiac responses; β2 blockade may worsen bronchospasm.
It is used to treat a feline with hyperthyroidism-mediated hypertension

pharm-e2-cardio14-008.prompt: What are pimobendan's two principal actions?
pharm-e2-cardio14-008.why: It is an inodilator: increases contractility while producing vasodilation because it opens K+ channels in vascular smooth muscle.

pharm-e2-resp15-020.prompt: Why must horses not receive zilpaterol-containing feed?
pharm-e2-resp15-020.answer: Zilpaterol is a beta-agonist that's approved in cattle, but can lead to lameness and health issues. It is highly toxic to equines.
pharm-e2-resp15-020.why: U.S. cattle-feed labeling explicitly prohibits equine access. Voluntarily withdrawn from cattle.

It is used for selected equine airway disease, with food-animal and competition limits
.

β2 stimulation may cause sweating, tremors, tachycardia or excitement.
Lasts 6-8 hours and has been abused in racehorses but there is no cardiopulmonary advantage for this.

pharm-e2-resp15-030.why:

pharm-e2-resp15-017.prompt: What makes ipratropium useful as an inhaled bronchodilator?
pharm-e2-resp15-017.answer: Local muscarinic blockade with relatively limited systemic absorption. So fewer side effects and a better dilator than atropine.
pharm-e2-resp15-017.why:
Its quaternary structure limits CNS penetration.
Doesn't cross the BBB, so it is poorly absorbed after aerosolization (which is better since that means the fewer side effects).
pharm-e2-resp15-017.slide: Lecture 15 · submitted recall notes + clinically reviewed guidance

pharm-e2-gi17-audit-002.prompt: Ropinirole is a pro emesis drug, what is it and its MOA?
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-002.answer: It is a dopamine agonist used to induce vomiting in appropriately selected dogs. (Clevor) it is an eye drop form.
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-002.why: Inducing and suppressing emesis are opposite treatment goals; patient and ingestion safety must be assessed.

pharm-e2-gi17-audit-014.prompt: What is rifaximin's proposed role in hepatic encephalopathy?
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-014.answer: A poorly absorbed intestinal antimicrobial adjunct to reduce bacterial ammonia production.
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-014.why:
It addresses a gut contribution to neurologic disease, not the underlying hepatic defect.
With non-absorbed antibiotics, it decreases urease and bacteria, so less ammonia. Usually given with another ABX.

pharm-e2-gi17-audit-004.prompt: How does n-butylscopolammonium (Buscopan) affect equine spasmodic colic?
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-004.answer: It blocks muscarinic signaling, relaxing GI smooth muscle.
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-004.why: Short-term reduction in spasm does not rule out impaction, ischemia, or surgical disease.

pharm-e2-94.prompt: Why is misoprostol used in selected GI injury?
pharm-e2-94.answer: As a prostaglandin E1 analogue supporting mucosal defenses. The PGE 1 receptor agonist decreases acid and increases bicarbonate and stomach mucus.
pharm-e2-94.why: Pregnancy and reproductive risks require caution. It is an abortifacient. Must wear gloves! Can also get rid of IUDs (depending on the brand!)

pharm-e2-96.prompt: What molecular target does fuzapladib (Panoquell CA-1) affect?
pharm-e2-96.answer: It is a LFA-1 Inhibitor- which decreases neutrophil migration into the pancreas to help reduce inflammation.
pharm-e2-96.why:
It is not an anti-NGF monoclonal antibody which it is often confused for. 
Used for recurrent pancreatitis as it destroys the islet cells, which can predispose to diabetes mellitus. So this helps prevent it. 
(I have also seen DVM's in practice give it to help with less hospitalization and they APPEAR to work but there is not enough published data to utilize this atm)

pharm-e2-gi17-audit-005.prompt: How do omeprazole and sucralfate differ in ulcer treatment?
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-005.answer: Omeprazole inhibits parietal H+/K+-ATPase; sucralfate provides local mucosal protection via increasing PGS
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-005.why: Acid suppression and surface protection address different aspects of injury.

pharm-e2-gi17-audit-009.prompt: What is fuzapladib's (Panoquell) pharmacologic class and target?
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-009.answer: It is a small-molecule LFA-1 inhibitor, not a monoclonal antibody.
pharm-e2-gi17-audit-009.why: The mechanism alters leukocyte adhesion; do not claim established prevention of recurrent pancreatitis.

pharm-e2-93.answer: Local mucosal protection at damaged surfaces.
pharm-e2-93.why: It does not inhibit acid secretion like a proton-pump inhibitor. Instead it provides a cyto-adherent coating on an ucler and increases GI prostaglandins.

pharm-e2-92.prompt: How can low-dose erythromycin stimulate GI movement?
pharm-e2-92.why: Motility therapy must be tailored to the underlying syndrome. At its regular dose, it does not have any GI motility advantage.

custom.prompt: What does the endothelium form and what does it maintain?
custom.answer:
Forms the BBB and maintains a nonthrombogenic boundary to prevent blood clot formation. Regulates hemostasis. Participates in the inflammatory response.
Actively transports molecules that the brain consumes rapidly and in large quanities (amino acids, glucose)

custom.prompt: What are the portals of entry for the CNS?
custom.answer: Direct extension, hematogenous, leukocyte trafficking, and retrograde axonal transport.
custom.why:
The most common is hematogenous. 
Direct extension is penetrative trauma or extension from the inner ear, bone, or nasal cavity. 
Leukocyte trafficking includes macrophages and lymphoid cells
and the retrograde axonal transport is infectious etiologies.

custom.prompt: What is Somogyi effect?
custom.answer: An overdose of insulin causes a rapid fall in glucose, then a rebound with a cyclic pattern.
custom.why:
Critical in the disease management of DM. 
Cyclic up-and-down pattern for 1-2 days of good control, then several poor days. 
Detected with a glucose curve.
TX: Reduce the dose!

custom.prompt: What is important to remember regarding checking blood glucose levels with DM?
custom.answer: Checking BG at multiple time points is critical
custom.why:
Spot checking at certain time frames means you could miss a problem! 
Difficult to do in cats due to epinephrine response. However, long acting glucose monitors are becoming more common and help mitigate this.

custom.prompt: What is a glucose nadir?
custom.answer: It is the lowest blood glucose reading after a meal or insulin dose.
custom.why: Knowing how low blood sugar drops helps determine whether an insulin or medication dose can be safely increased without causing dangerously low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Even if readings are high at other times, a low nadir warns against raising the dose

custom.prompt: What is the difference between amorphous and crystalline insulin?
custom.answer:
Amorphous is regular insulin with no excipients--> fast absorption but short duration
Crystallin contains an excipient --> slow absorption, longer duration
custom.why: Helps to determine action and duration. Experiments allow for slower absorption due to the binding of the cyrstals/ matrix

custom.prompt: Which two drugs address ventricular ectopic beats (PVC's) and what is their MOA?
custom.answer:
Verapamill and diltiazem
Class IV: Ca2+ channel blockers
custom.why: Verapamil is IV for short-term use and diltiazem is oral for long-term use.

custom.prompt: What two drugs and class are useful for treating ventricular dysrhythmias (not atrial problems), and what is the MOA?

Lidocaine and mexiletine
Na+ channel blockers that bind rapidly and selectively to refractory channels. (Fast on and off)
custom.why:
Lidocaine is IV for severe acute ventricular arrhythmias, and mexiletine is an oral syrup for long-term use.

custom.prompt: What is the MOA for hydralazine and why it is only used in emergency situations?
custom.answer: It decreases Ca release from the SR and increases NO sensitivity and opens K+ channgels in vascular smooth muscle. It causes so much hypotension that the baroreflex leads to tachycardia.
custom.why: Another anti-hypertensive drug is Sodium nitroprusside, as it is a NO donor activating the NANC pathway, so you get vasodilation, which is another emergency option.

custom.prompt: What are the antiarrhythmics that we discussed in lecture?
custom.answer: Lidocaine, Mexiletine, Procainamide, Propranolol, Amiodarone, Verapamil, and Diltiazem

custom.prompt: What are the anti CHF drugs?
custom.answer: Digoxin, Dopamine, Dobutamine, Amrinone, Pimobendan

custom.prompt: What are the antihypertensive and resuscitative drugs? (How it was grouped)

custom.prompt: What are the Bronchodilators (Beta agnosits) mentioned in the lecture?
custom.answer: Epinephrine, ephedrine, isoproterenol, Terbutaline, Albuterol (salbuterol), Clenbuterol, and Zilpaterol
custom.why: B2 causes bronchodilation, B1 tachycardia, alpha activity is non selective and can cause hypertension

custom.prompt: What are the methlxanthines listed in this lecture?
custom.answer: Theophylline and aminophylline

custom.prompt: What is the difference between theophylline and aminophylline?
custom.answer: They are fairly similar; the major difference is that aminophylline is often used for bronchodilation in small animals.
custom.why:
Both are PDE inhibitors that raise cAMP --> interfere with Ca2+ mobilization --> bronchodilation.
They are also an adenosine receptor antagonsits which can cause alertness and bronchodilation.
Decrease mast cell degranulation, increase mucociliary clearance, and can decrease diaphragm function, increase pulmonary artery pressure, and increase CNS sensitivity to PaCO2.

custom.prompt: What are the two drugs to address hepatic encephalopathy?
custom.answer: Lactulose and Rifaximin.
custom.why:
Lactulose is fermented by bacteria and acidifies the gut, so NH3 is trapped as NH4+ and not absorbed.
Rifazimin is a non-absorbed ABX so it decreases urease and bacteria so less NH3

custom.prompt: What are the three main anti emetics?
custom.answer: Metoclopramide (Reglan), Maropitant (Cerenia), and Ondansetron.
custom.why:
Metoclopramide is a D2 antagonist (also helps with gut motility)
Maripitant is an NK1 antagonist
Ondansetron is a 5-HT3 antagonist.

custom.prompt: What is benthanechol used for in terms of GI and what is its other function?
custom.answer: It is a muscarinic agnoist, so it causes urination and helps as an equine prokinetic
custom.why: Helpful to remember multiple drug functions to understand side effects

custom.prompt: What are the fours anti-colic therapies for horses and their function?
custom.answer:
Magnesium sulfate is an osmotic agent and helps with impacts that are less than 3 days.
Mineral oil is a lubricant and decreases water reabsorption
Pysllium helps with bulk and aids to clear sand impaction
Buscopan (N-butylscopolammonium) is a muscarinic antagonist and helps relax the GI tract
